record.one_liner: Meta's microblogging social network, whose API lets apps publish posts, read profiles and media, moderate replies, search, and pull insights on behalf of users.
record.auth_notes: Authorization-window flow: the authorization code is valid 1 hour and is exchanged for a short-lived token (1 hour), then a long-lived token (60 days). Refresh with GET /refresh_access_token. Tokens are app-scoped per app/user pair. Permissions: threads_basic, threads_content_publish, threads_manage_replies, threads_read_replies, threads_manage_insights, plus threads_delete and threads_location_tagging (named on the overview page). Use the Threads app ID and secret, not the generic Meta app ID and secret.
record.access_notes: Creating a Meta app with the Threads use case is free. Users with a role on the app (Threads Testers) can grant permissions without review. Users without a role can grant permissions only after each permission passes App Review and the app is published. I did not fetch the App Review page, so its details (such as business verification) are unverified. One community server README mentions business verification; I did not confirm this in Meta docs.
record.blocker: App Review is required for each permission before users outside the app's tester roles can connect. Other limits: 60-day tokens that need refreshing, 250 API posts per profile per 24h, 1,000 replies per 24h, and 500-character text posts. The API is Graph-style HTTP, and the docs do not call it REST. Meta publishes no official MCP server.
